        "Same-server copies now use EWS CopyItem instead of the cross-server streaming handler; moves retain MoveItem. Historical common callbacks map returned IDs by request order after a cardinality guard, create local destination headers and delete source headers only when isMove. Legacy versions request a destination sync instead of relying on returned IDs. Current renamed Exchange code retains this route and explicit fallback; later undo, safe-listener and error guards are current context, not authored coverage of this entry.",

CopyItems bridge returns after spawning the operation; remote completion is carried by callbacks/listeners, not the initial NS_OK/Ok.",

The original new copy test checks source/destination counts and fake-server folder membership for old/new IDs, but never asserts the EWS ID on destination local headers. Current fake instead returns newItemIds. This static mismatch and coverage limit are kept separate from real Exchange behavior or a reproduced failure.",
        "Original new copy assertions all have non-empty should messages and check6scalar outcomes. The tests wait for destination count2, not the copy listener or complete metadata. Current refactored copy subtest adds subject checks and awaits a copy listener/notifications, but testCopyItemEws and testCopyItemGraph invoke that async helper without await/return; they do not pass its completion to the task promise. This is a later accepted-source test gap, not introduced by the original direct test and not a fresh failure.",

Reporter intends same-account CopyItem to preserve server metadata absent from RFC message headers, compared with prior CreateItem. Actual source chooses CopyItem for same-server copy, but these tests and static code do not certify metadata fidelity or cross-account support.",

Landed comments now say copy or move; helper JSDoc says prefix names folders/items, not the operation mode. The actual helper spelling is setup_item_copymove_structure, so the suggested setup_copymove_item_structure is not treated as exact adoption. A double-space nit in the Rust conversion comment is formatting, not a new architecture rule.",

Early rustfmt reports and build failures, later diff updates/completions and Try link remain historical. Nothing in the review specifically validates the fake returned-ID mismatch or current unawaited wrappers; these remain independent exact-source findings, not reviewer-diagnosed failures.",
